rows.en:
……Now, I wonder how many people in the whole world own a Rubelize?
If anyone were to cut her wish short, it would have to be someone, somewhere, who owns a Rubelize, saying this:
"Please make everyone in the world happy."
But could that ever really happen?
Think about it.
Would people who own a Rubelize, a stone no ordinary person could ever get, wish for everyone's happiness?
Surely they'd make the same wish Okawa did.
And the stronger that desire grows, the unhappier everyone becomes.{p}

……Heh heh heh.
There's a saying, isn't there? 'Other people's misfortune tastes like honey.'
If everyone became unhappy, that might be a kind of happiness in its own way.
As for me, I'm fine as long as no harm comes to me.
……{a}{f:|}.
You'd better be careful too.
Even while you sit here listening to scary stories, all sorts of things are happening around you.
Don't forget that Okawa is at our school.
What misfortune visits you is entirely up to her.
Heh heh heh heh……
In the end, the seventh one never came.
I suppose that means this gathering is over.
What a shame that nothing happened.
There did seem to be a sign that something might happen, though……
Well, never mind.
I may simply have been mistaken.{p}Well then, everyone.
Shall we bring this to a close?{p}

I see.
So you say there's no such thing as fate.
But the world is full of all kinds of accidents, isn't it?
Or chances that come out of nowhere.
And meetings with other people.
There certainly are things we can't foresee.
Some people call that chance.
But if we were to call it fate instead……{p}
Do you think you could somehow change that fate?

I see.
You say that very plainly, don't you?{p}

I see……
Life isn't all good things, is it?
I wonder if that's fate too.
If so, then perhaps reaching for happiness is really an unconscious attempt to defy fate.{p}

Heh heh……
The story I'm about to tell you is a story about fate.{p}

That's right.
Okawa went to the Okazaki home to get them to hand the Rubelize over to her.
But the way she put it was so sly.
She told them it was a cursed stone, so it mustn't be left in the grave with Okazaki.
Then she said she would dispose of the Rubelize, and asked them to leave the rest to her.
"Please trust me and let me take care of the Rubelize."
That's what Okawa asked of them.{p}So how do you think Okazaki's parents answered?
All right
Don't mess with us!

"All right.
Please do……"
That's how Okazaki's parents answered.
Then they said they would take the Rubelize out of the grave soon, and asked how they could contact her.
Okawa was overjoyed and gave them her address and phone number.
And then, about three days later……{p}

There was a phone call at Okawa's house.
"Is this Okawa?
……This is Yukie Okazaki's father.
Thank you for the other day.
The Rubelize really is cursed, isn't it?
We dug up the grave after that, but……
One of the men doing the work slipped and fell into the hole we'd dug.{p}

He hit his head and died.
……Okawa.
I've already sent the Rubelize to you.
Please, see that it gets a proper memorial……"
Just then, she heard the doorbell ring at the front door.
…………{p}
Let me tell you a little about Yukie Okazaki now.{p}

She was a girl from a perfectly ordinary family.
But apparently the son and heir of a certain wealthy zaibatsu family gave her a Rubelize.
They say even at the prices back then it cost as much as a house, so it was a present far beyond anything we'd think of as normal.
The zaibatsu boy's name was Hideto Fujiomi.
Fujiomi had been in love with Okazaki for a long time, without her returning it.
He gave her the Rubelize and confessed, asking her to go out with him.
Okazaki was a very pretty girl.
She had a distinctive kind of cuteness, the kind that could have made her an idol.
Her classmates were all envious.
Back then, no one cared yet about Rubelize being a stone that brings happiness.
But since it was a rare stone even by world standards, it seems it became the talk of the school.
So the girls who told Okawa about her must have heard that rumor from somewhere too.{p}

Fujiomi had the Rubelize made into a pendant and gave it to Okazaki.
And then he told her this.
That Rubelize was a stone that brings happiness.
That it would grant any wish at all.
And that this was to be a secret between just the two of them……
Okazaki told herself
that he'd simply meant it as a bit of good-luck magic.
And then Fujiomi……
He stared at her intently and said something like this.
"Why don't we test the Rubelize's power……?"
His eyes were so serious that she caught her breath for a moment.
But Fujiomi took her hand and went on.
"We've got an English test today, right?
Hold the Rubelize and cast a little charm.
Wish that you'll get a good score."
He smiled gently.
Seeing that, Okazaki relaxed.
"I'll give it a try," she answered lightly.{p}

And then, second period.
The English test was given.
The answer sheets were handed out, and Okazaki held her breath.
"Ah……!"{p}

The answers were faintly rising up on her answer sheet.
(Wh-what is this……?)
She was astonished.
It didn't take her long to realize it was the Rubelize's power.
"How was it?
The test?"
The moment the test was over, Fujiomi came straight over to talk to her.
Okazaki answered him with trembling lips.
"It really worked……"
Seeing the state she was in, Fujiomi smiled with satisfaction.
And he slowly nodded.{p}

"I see.
So this stone really is……"
The two of them faced each other and fell silent.
After a while, Fujiomi said this.
"Okazaki, want to test it one more time?"
She had no reason to say no.{p}
……And the next day.{p}

At Fujiomi's suggestion, she was going to pray for the weather to change.
"There's no way a wish like that could come true, is there?"
Even as she said that, her heart was bubbling with excitement.
At lunch break on a clear, sunny day, Okazaki went outside, clutched the Rubelize tight, and prayed.
"Please change today's weather……"{p}

Then all of a sudden the sky lit up,
and lightning struck.
"Eek, aaaaaaah!☆"
Okazaki was so startled that she slammed into the railing.
"Ow!"
Fujiomi got a real fright too.
For a while the two of them huddled close together, shaking violently.
"F-Fujiomi……"
Okazaki looked at him, her eyes on the verge of tears.
……He was smiling.{p}

"Fuji……omi……?"
She suddenly felt afraid.
After all, his smile was twisted into something eerie……
"Okazaki……"
Fujiomi slowly opened his mouth.
And he said this.
"There's something I want to ask of you……"{p}What do you think he wanted to ask of her?
Actually, there's someone I want to kill
There's one more thing I want to test

"Y-you don't mean there's actually someone you want to kill……?"
She faltered.
Then Fujiomi's jaw dropped.
"Okazaki, what are you thinking?"
He clapped her on the shoulder.
But……
even as he said it, a sinister shadow lurked deep in his eyes.
"Oh, come on, this is ridiculous.
I bet that lightning just now was a coincidence too."
Despite having said he had something to ask her, he suddenly walked off on his own.
"W-wait!☆"
Okazaki hurried after him.
And she apologized.
She said she was sorry for saying something so strange.{p}
Then, a few days later……{p}

Okazaki's Rubelize went missing.
Well, rather than missing……
To put it simply, it was stolen.
That's not especially surprising, is it?
Everyone knew she had a rare gem called a Rubelize, after all.
It's only natural that someone would try to steal it.
Ever since the lightning, Okazaki had left the Rubelize in her bag the whole time.
Because it had come to seem like a truly frightening stone to her.
And then, before long, it was stolen.
She regretted it; she should have kept it on her at all times.
And she began avoiding Fujiomi.
She felt guilty about losing the Rubelize.
Then, one day……{p}

Okazaki got a phone call at home from Fujiomi.
He said he hated how awkward things had gotten between them lately.
……Okazaki thought it over.
She would apologize to him.
She would tell him honestly about the stone.{p}

The two of them met at the school at night.
And Okazaki said this to Fujiomi.
"Fujiomi…… I'm sorry.
The truth is, I lost the Rubelize……"
Okazaki told him honestly.
And then……{p}
"Aaaaaaaaaah!☆"{p}
She felt a violent pain in her chest, coughed up blood, and collapsed.{p}

"Gurgh…… gagh……"
Pitch-black liquid poured from her mouth, mixed in with the blood.
……Fujiomi was laughing.
"Heh heh, Okazaki.{p}

I'm the one who stole the Rubelize.
Only you and I know about the Rubelize's power, right?
So I decided to shut you up.
From here on, I'm going to graduate from a good university and land a good job.
With the stone's power.
I was worried that using the stone's power might bring something horrible as the price, but……
it looks like that's not a problem.
At the test, and when we changed the weather, no disaster befell you, the one who made the wishes.
Now I'll put my real goal to the test.
Okazaki.
I want to kill you.{p}

You never even looked at me until I gave you the Rubelize, did you?
You knew how I felt, and you still brushed me off coldly.
And now look at you.
The moment I gave you a jewel, you start acting like my girlfriend?
I don't need a girl like that.
With the Rubelize's power, I'll make myself a much better girlfriend……"
Fujiomi's eyes were so vacant you couldn't tell where he was looking.{p}

"Gh…… gaaah……"
Groaning, Okazaki clawed at the ground again and again.
On the ground lay a pool of the blood and filth that had come out of her mouth……
It clung to her nails and fingertips, sticky and slimy.
Even so, she clawed at the ground over and over.{p}

So she could drag herself along.
So she could reach out for Fujiomi……
"S-stop it……☆"
Fujiomi staggered back in terror and slipped in her filth.
And he dropped the Rubelize.{p}
Okazaki snatched it up in an instant.{p}
And then……{p}

"Wh……waaaaaaaah!☆"
…………{p}

The next day, Okazaki's body was found at the school gate.
They say Fujiomi's body was lying beside hers.{p}

In Okazaki's hand, the Rubelize pendant was clutched tight.
With the last of her strength, she must have made a wish to the Rubelize.
That she wanted revenge on him……
……The two bodies were clean.
The blood and filth Okazaki should have vomited had vanished without a trace.
The police came and looked into all sorts of things, but in the end they decided the two had probably killed themselves.
Because the two of them had died huddled together, just as if it were a lovers' suicide.
No one knew why they'd killed themselves, but the two must surely have been deeply in love.
That was the rumor that went around.
Some people even said it was rather dramatic.
And so the story became that Okazaki had been happy right up until she died.
The school even held a staff meeting over it, calling it a mistake brought on by immature teenage hearts.
But the truth is different.
What killed them was the stone's power……
The power of a stone that controls fate had led their hearts astray……{p}

"Delivery!☆
Delivery!☆"
A young man's voice.
The sound of knocking on the door.{p}

Okawa opened the door.
Telling herself all the while that the Rubelize being cursed was surely a lie.
Heh heh……
The Rubelize that reached Okawa really was cursed.
After all, the grudge from Okazaki's death had attached itself to it.
The wish she made as she was dying lingered strongly in the stone.
You remember what she wished on Fujiomi, don't you?
"I'll kill you……"
So Okawa fell victim to it too.{p}

From what I hear, she was killed by the young man who delivered the Rubelize.
The man who killed her is to be pitied too, isn't he?
All he did was carry the Rubelize, and he ended up committing a crime he never saw coming.
They say the police took him away.
I wonder if that's fate too.
What is fate, I wonder?
What do you think, {a}{f:|}……?{p}

That's right.
Okazaki's parents told her not to mess with them and threw her out.{p}

……But Okawa couldn't give up.
So at last she made up her mind.
She would secretly dig up Okazaki's grave.
What kind of nerves did she have, I wonder?
She seemed to think it was fine to steal from the dead as long as no one found out.
Okawa waited for the dead of night, then put her plan into action.{p}

I think graveyards are frightening even in the daytime.
And this was the middle of the night.
A high school girl, all alone.
That's not something just anyone could do.
And her purpose was grave robbing, at that.
Okawa must have had nerves of steel.
Or perhaps the Rubelize sleeping in the grave was calling her to it.
Heh heh……
Either way, she moved the gravestone aside and took Okazaki's urn out from inside.{p}

"Actually, there's one more thing I want to test."
That's what Fujiomi said.
All the while staring at Okazaki with glittering eyes that gleamed from somewhere deep inside.
"Wh-what is it?"
Okazaki asked him.
His manner was creepy, but it was none other than Fujiomi who had given her the Rubelize.
She felt he had every right to use it.
Fujiomi grinned and said,
"Will you come with me after school today?"{p}How do you think Okazaki answered?
Sure
Sorry, I have something to do

"Sure."
Okazaki nodded.{p}

Then after school that day, the two of them went to the main road near the school.
Fujiomi took her by the hand and led her up onto the pedestrian bridge.
Okazaki was uneasy, because she couldn't understand what he was doing.
"What are you planning to do?"
And then, wouldn't you know it, Fujiomi said happily:
"My older brother is about to come down this road.
What I wish for is his death."
Okazaki couldn't believe her ears.
After all, wanting to kill your own brother isn't something a sane person thinks of.
But Fujiomi's expression was serious.
The mood didn't allow her to say a word.
While Okazaki hesitated, Fujiomi's eyes lit up.
"Here he comes!"
She looked, and a red convertible was speeding toward them from the far end.
Fujiomi raised the hand holding the Rubelize high in the air.
"Death to my brother!"{p}

When she heard that, Okazaki's body began to move on its own.
She climbed onto the railing of the pedestrian bridge and looked down at the road.
She couldn't believe what she herself was doing.
Her body was moving on its own……
As Okazaki trembled, Fujiomi spoke to her from behind.{p}

"My real wish, you see, is for my brother to die without my ever getting my hands dirty.
You're going to jump from here.
And my brother will get caught up in it and die.
Well then, goodbye, Okazaki."
……He said it in a tone as if he were saying 'see you tomorrow.'
And as if that were the signal, Okazaki jumped.{p}

……Okazaki's body slammed straight into the red car.
The shock made the driver jerk the wheel the wrong way, and the car plowed into the guardrail.
And right there was a group of elementary schoolchildren walking home from school together.
They say it turned into a horrible catastrophe.
You know the crosswalk on the way to school?
That was put in after the pedestrian bridge was torn down back then.
So that no more students would try to kill themselves there.
……That's right.{p}

Okazaki's death was ruled a sudden, impulsive suicide.
Fujiomi, who had been with her, wasn't suspected of anything.
Was this the Rubelize's power too, I wonder?
Oh yes, about the cause of Okazaki's death.
There seem to be all sorts of rumors.
Some say it was an accident, and some even say she was murdered.
Well, rumors are only rumors in the end.
The police said Okazaki's death was suicide.
Fujiomi was never charged with anything.
That alone is the truth.
What became of Fujiomi afterward?
With his brother gone, I imagine he became heir to the zaibatsu.
You can call it unfair, but there's nothing to be done about it.
The Rubelize can't tell good from evil, after all.
It only granted a wish.
Isn't that so?{p}

Okawa crept fearfully toward the front door.
(The Rubelize's arrived.
What do I do? It can't really be cursed, can it? He must be wrong……)
But even thinking that, she couldn't shake a bad feeling.
"Nobody home?
Um, excuse me……!"{p}

Okawa opened the door with trembling hands.
"Oh, hello. Delivery for you."{p}

A small package.
It was the Rubelize, all right.
Can you guess what happened to Okawa after that?
The Rubelize truly was a cursed stone.
After all, it had been shut up in the grave for so long with Okazaki, who was murdered.
It must have heard a great many bitter words from her.
For example…… let me see.{p}

"I'll get my revenge,"
or
"I'll kill you,"
things like that……
That stone had soaked up all sorts of Okazaki's feelings.
And the moment it left the grave, it let all that grudge loose.
They say Okawa was found dead in her room the next day.
The cause is unknown, apparently.
Her body had no wounds, and she hadn't been ill to begin with, either.{p}
